turns.user: What is the Cape Cod Rail Resilience Project?

response.reply: The Cape Cod Rail Resilience Project is an initiative aimed at improving rail safety and climate resilience along the Cape Main Line by integrating advanced technology with stakeholder-driven research methods [1]. The project, which was inspired by the doctoral research of project lead Carlos Velásquez, addresses the increasing risks climate change poses to critical transportation infrastructure [1]. Carlos Velásquez serves as a project manager at MassDOT and is a PhD candidate at UMass Boston [1]. The project was launched in response to a 300-foot rail embankment collapse that occurred in East Sandwich in 2020, an event linked to climate change-induced drought conditions [1]. Supported by USDOT funding, the team utilizes drones for mapping and sensors to monitor water levels [1]. This collaborative effort brings together experts from MassDOT, UMass Boston, and AECOM [1]. The project’s innovative approach combines aerial surveys, hydrological drought analysis, and real-time monitoring systems at three pilot study sites [1].
